title: Modi Jets Off on Six-Day, Five-Nation Energy Blitz
excerpt: PM departs May 15 for UAE, Netherlands, Sweden, Norway and Italy as Middle East crisis squeezes India's oil lifelines
body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi departs Thursday on a six-day, five-nation tour — from May 15 to 20, spanning the UAE and four European capitals — on what New Delhi is framing as a mission for energy security, trade, and technology at a moment of acute geopolitical pressure.

**Energy first, Abu Dhabi stop:**
Modi's first destination is the UAE, where he meets President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan to advance the bilateral Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and exchange views on the West Asia conflict. The stakes are high: the UAE is India's fifth-largest source of fuel, accounting for almost 6 per cent of total crude imports, and the third-largest source of LPG and petroleum products. The escalating conflict in West Asia and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz have sent shockwaves through global energy markets, and this diplomatic marathon is being viewed as a 'mission for energy security.'

**Europe: trade deals and tech summits:**
This is the Indian Prime Minister's first visit to Europe since the announcement of the conclusion of negotiations for a free trade agreement earlier this year. Officials say the tour will focus heavily on trade, investment, green technology, defence cooperation, semiconductors, artificial intelligence and resilient supply chains, with the recently concluded India-EU Free Trade Agreement expected to dominate discussions across European capitals. In Oslo, Modi will participate in the 3rd India-Nordic Summit alongside leaders from Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Sweden and Norway, sharpening India's engagement with the Nordic bloc in clean energy, Arctic cooperation, blue economy and advanced technologies. The Norway stop will also mark the first time in 43 years that an Indian prime minister visits the country.

**What to watch:**
The multi-country tour is being viewed in diplomatic circles as one of India's most consequential outreach efforts to Europe in recent years — watch for the concrete agreements Modi signs on energy supply, semiconductor cooperation, and the India-EU FTA implementation timeline.

sources.label: Ministry of External Affairs (via Reuters / AL-Monitor)

nri_angle: With the India-EU Free Trade Agreement poised to open 93 per cent of Indian exports to European markets duty-free, Indian-American professionals and entrepreneurs with ties to India's export and technology sectors stand to see new business corridors unlock in real time.
